## Purpose and Product Surfaces
Caveman reduces AI-agent token use: skills shorten agent prose; a local proxy compresses agent input context while retaining recoverable originals. It is a multi-runtime monorepo spanning Node/TypeScript distribution and agent integration, Go runtime services, and Python/TypeScript SDK middleware.

Primary user entries are the npm installer (`bin/install.js`), CLI (`packages/cli/src/index.ts`), and Go service binaries: proxy, engine, MCP, shrink, browse, and memory.

## CLI, Installation, and Agent Wrapping
The TypeScript CLI coordinates setup, persistent/ephemeral agent wrapping, provider routing, local binary management, proxy requests, skills, telemetry, stats, and learning workflows. Agent profiles are declarative inputs compiled into generated CLI registries; wrappers avoid mutating source agent configuration where possible.

Paths: `packages/cli/src/index.ts`, `bin/install.js`, `agents/profiles/schema.json`, `agents/compile.mjs`.

Control flow: install/setup discovers installed agents and binaries → profile-selected wrapper configures environment or temporary config → launches the agent against the local proxy and optional MCP/browse/shrink tools.

## Proxy Gateway and Provider Boundary
`caveman-proxy` is the primary runtime boundary between an agent and upstream LLM APIs. Its gateway accepts provider-compatible requests, identifies provider/auth mode, applies compression, caching/pixel/tool-schema policies, forwards upstream, handles streaming/retries, and records usage/evidence. Provider adapters preserve each wire protocol and credential model for Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible services, Gemini, Bedrock, Vertex, and Azure OpenAI.

Paths: `proxy/cmd/caveman-proxy/main.go`, `proxy/internal/gateway/proxy.go`, `proxy/internal/gateway/server.go`, `proxy/providers/adapter.go`, `proxy/routing/routing.go`.

External boundaries: local agent clients; upstream Anthropic, OpenAI, Google/Gemini, AWS Bedrock, Vertex AI, Azure/OpenRouter-compatible endpoints; AWS credential/signing support.

## Compression Engine and Recoverability
The Go engine detects payload type and dispatches specialized compressors for JSON, logs, code, diffs, HTML, terminal output, tool schemas, tabular data, search results, and text. It returns compressed context plus metadata needed to retrieve originals. Context-window packing ranks candidate content by relevance/recency/error signal under a token budget.

Paths: `engine/engine.go`, `engine/detect.go`, `engine/compressors/compressor.go`, `engine/contextwindow/contextwindow.go`, `engine/ccr/store.go`.

The CCR layer is a local SQLite-backed content/recovery store with locking, permission, generation, and deduplication controls. This separates lossy prompt optimization from byte-exact source recovery.

## MCP and Local Tool Ecosystem
The MCP server exposes engine functions to any MCP host: compression, original retrieval, stats, and TOON encode/decode. Standalone tools reuse related runtime capabilities: `shrink` compresses subprocess output; `browse` drives Chrome/CDP and produces compressed page context; `mem` provides durable BM25-backed recall.

Paths: `mcp/cmd/caveman-mcp/main.go`, `mcp/server.go`, `shrink/cmd/caveman-shrink/main.go`, `browse/cmd/caveman-browse/main.go`, `mem/store.go`.

## Agent Runtime, Skills, and SDK Integration
The agent package provides a TypeScript execution kernel with adapters, budgets, context IR/definition/source graphs, compaction, memory, and sandboxed tool execution. Skills and plugins are the lightweight behavior layer installed into many agent ecosystems; generated packs derive from registry/profile definitions. SDK and middleware packages let application developers route provider/framework calls through Caveman-compatible optimization and reporting interfaces.

Paths: `packages/agent/src/execution-kernel.ts`, `packages/agent/src/context-ir.ts`, `skills/registry.json`, `packages/middleware/typescript/src/transport.ts`, `packages/sdk/python/caveman_cloud/core.py`.

## Pixel and Representation Optimization
Pixel mode conditionally converts profitable skill text to image pages, using embedded glyph atlases and provider-specific request transforms. TOON is a compact structured-data representation with encode/decode support across engine, MCP, CLI, and proxy pathways.

Paths: `engine/pixel/gate.go`, `engine/pixel/transform_anthropic.go`, `engine/pixel/transform_openai.go`, `engine/compressors/toon.go`.

## Persistence, Learning, and Deployment
Proxy-side stores aggregate sessions, imported histories, compression savings, pricing, experiments, and recommendations for `learn`, `stats`, and trial workflows. Local-first operation uses SQLite and filesystem state; shared deployment supports Docker Compose, Kubernetes, and AWS ECS. Shared Go platform packages centralize security, redaction, SSRF protection, telemetry, object storage, KMS, and provider catalog concerns.

Paths: `proxy/internal/store/store.go`, `proxy/internal/store/learn.go`, `deploy/docker-compose.yml`, `deploy/kubernetes.yaml`, `shared/platform/redact/redact.go`.
